content: 1. Minimize the spillage of materials and reduce dust emissions during handling and application processes. 2. Ensure that seeds are sown at the recommended seeding rate to optimize growth and minimize waste. 3. To protect birds and mammals, all treated seeds must be completely covered with soil, including at the ends of rows. 4. After sowing, do not leave empty seed bags or leftover treated seeds in the environment. Dispose of them in accordance with local regulations. 5. Any leftover treated seeds should be returned to their original bags, and empty seed bags must not be repurposed for other uses. For Baits: 6. Clean up any spillage of bait immediately to prevent unintended exposure. 7. Baits must be securely placed to minimize the risk of consumption by non-target animals. Secure bait blocks to prevent rodents from dragging them away. 8. Clearly mark the treatment area during the treatment period to ensure safety and awareness. 9. Remove dead rodents from the treatment area daily during the treatment period. Do not dispose of them in refuse bins or rubbish tips. 10. Remove all bait materials once the treatment is completed to prevent environmental contamination. Care of Equipment: 11. Maintain application equipment in good condition, ensuring it is free from leaks and external contamination. Clean the equipment regularly to ensure proper functioning. Hazard Colour Bands: 12. Hazard classifications, as defined by the Globally Harmonized System (GHS) or the World Health Organization (WHO), are associated with specific hazard colour bands. These bands are coded using the Pantone Matching System (PMS) and should be printed horizontally at the bottom of product labels. 13. The responsible authority in each country should assign colour bands based on either the GHS or WHO classification system, but the two systems should not be mixed. GHS Acute Toxicity Classifications: Category 1: Fatal if swallowed, in contact with skin, or inhaled. Colour band: PMS Red 199 C. Category 2: Fatal if swallowed, in contact with skin, or inhaled. Colour band: PMS Red 199 C. Category 3: Toxic if swallowed, in contact with skin, or inhaled. Colour band: PMS Yellow C. Category 4: Harmful if swallowed, in contact with skin, or inhaled. Colour band: PMS Blue 293 C. Category 5: May be harmful if swallowed, in contact with skin, or inhaled. Colour band: PMS Green 347 C. WHO Acute Toxicity Classifications: Class Ia: Extremely hazardous. Colour band: PMS Red 199 C. Class Ib: Highly hazardous. Colour band: PMS Red 199 C. Class II: Moderately hazardous. Colour band: PMS Yellow C. Class III: Slightly hazardous. Colour band: PMS Blue 293 C. Class U: Unlikely to present acute hazard in normal use. Colour band: PMS Green 347 C. Precautionary Pictograms: 14. Pictograms should be printed in black and white and placed at the bottom of the label. Their size should be appropriate for the label, with a preferred size of approximately 15 mm x 15 mm for bottles of 1 to 5 liters, but never smaller than 7 mm x 7 mm. 15. Pictograms must correspond to the specific safety precautions required for the product. For example, gloves and eye protection should be worn when handling concentrated liquids, while gloves, boots, and washing after use may be required for ready-to-use products. 16. Pictograms should be grouped and enclosed in clearly defined boxes to indicate their association with specific activities or advice. Supplementary Information on Pictograms: 17. Pesticide distributors, retailers, and outlets should provide users with information about the meaning of the pictograms on labels. This information can be provided in brochures, leaflets, or laminated cards, preferably in the language(s) understood by the users. 18. Such informational materials can also be included in the pesticide packaging to ensure users are well-informed about safety precautions.
